reversibility_invariant: REMOVE is not a representable outcome; every DISABLE is undone by re-enabling one JSON key. Route disables through mcpapply's DISABLE_PREFERENCE (project-scoped): a disable written to root disabledMcpServers hides the tools but does NOT prevent the spawn, so it saves zero RAM (mcpapply/plan.py SPAWN_PREVENTING).

signals.host_reachable: claude mcp list (NOT a mount signal)
signals.session_mounted: mcp__* namespaces in the auditing session
signals.call_verified: S4 union: a real call succeeded by EITHER method -- a stdio initialize+tools/list handshake, or a real in-session tool call. Read call_method for which one, handshake_verified/s4_executed for the halves. Enforced by assert_signal_consistency(). SCOPE, and it is narrower than 'the server works': call_method='stdio-handshake' proves the PROCESS starts and ADVERTISES a tool surface; it does not prove any tool executes. Counter-example executed 2026-08-13 by the integrate lane -- searxng ships handshake_verified=true with 4 tools, while a real in-session searxng_instance_info call returned available=false, its backing instance at 127.0.0.1:8890 unreachable. call_method='in-session-tool-call' IS the stronger evidence. A consumer must not read this field as capability-in-use.
signals.s4_executed: S4b only: (tool, result) of a real in-session tool call
signals.call_method: which S4 method answered, or null if neither. A row where BOTH answered reads 'stdio-handshake+in-session-tool-call': reporting only the handshake discarded the in-session call the legend itself calls the stronger evidence.
signals.backend_liveness: Per-BACKEND liveness for a proxy row. A server-level signal cannot express 'the server is up and this backend is not', which is exactly what cloud-hub does: it keeps advertising a dead backend's tools and says so itself -- "Its other tools stay listed". probed[] carries one real read-only call per backend with its verdict; unprobed[] is UNMEASURED and explicitly NOT claimed live. tools_over_dead_backend is attributed via backend_map, whose C1 completeness control proves every cloud-hub name classifies; it is null for any server without such a map -- null means NOT ATTRIBUTED, never zero. A dead backend does not shrink call_verified: the call really did succeed. It shrinks what that success is evidence OF.
signals.liveness_basis: Whether pid/rss_bytes/tool_count/name_bytes/schema_bytes on THIS row were sampled from a real stdio child, or were not measured and why. A row whose basis starts with 'not-measured:' carries no liveness snapshot and must NOT be injected into mcpctl.matrix.Liveness. Enforced by assert_liveness_consistency().
signals.last_error: a stdio handshake that was ATTEMPTED and FAILED. Null on a row with no stdio command at all -- that case is probe_note, because a categorical 'nothing to spawn' is not a failure of the server.
signals.probe_note: why no stdio child was attempted (not an error)

refuted_round_1.claim: round 1 documented call_verified as 'real initialize+tools/list, or a real in-session tool call' while computing it from the handshake alone
refuted_round_1.measured: 5 rows (agent-mail, basic-memory, figma, github, huggingface) had call_verified=false beside their own non-null s4_executed evidence; the prose said 21/23 verified while the field summed to 16
refuted_round_1.fix: call_verified is now the union, call_method names the method, and assert_signal_consistency() aborts the run on the old shape

refuted_round_2.claim: round 2 wrote that disposition.json rows 'now also carry pid + rss_bytes, so a row of the shipped table IS an injectable snapshot'
refuted_round_2.measured: true for the 16 handshake-verified rows and false for the other 7, whose pid/rss_bytes/tool_count/name_bytes/schema_bytes are all null; 5 of those 7 additionally shipped call_verified=true beside last_error="transport='http': no stdio command", so an injected Liveness would have read verified-and-failed at once
refuted_round_2.fix: every row now carries liveness_basis; the categorical case moved to probe_note; assert_liveness_consistency() aborts the run on a verified-and-errored row, a missing basis, a basis that claims a measurement it does not have, and a reasonless not-measured
refuted_round_2.residual: the 7 rows still have no cost measurement. Settling experiment: an HTTP initialize+tools/list against each endpoint, or a dump of the client-side tool registry -- neither is a stdio spawn, so neither is reachable from this producer as built.

refuted_round_5.claim: the DISABLE row for searxng shipped 'all 4 tool names are a strict subset of search-hub's surface, 0 unique -- nothing becomes unreachable'
refuted_round_5.verdict: REFUTED as an OVERCLAIM; the disposition itself is unchanged
refuted_round_5.measured: 2026-08-13, real in-session calls to BOTH copies of searxng_instance_info returned byte-identical available=false against the same unreachable http://127.0.0.1:8890. The set arithmetic was correct; the sentence implied search-hub still SERVES the capability, and it does not -- there is no failover to fall back to
refuted_round_5.fix: the sentence is generated from shared_dead_resource(), which returns None for any pair without a jointly-measured dead resource and lets the plain wording ship. The byte-identity claim is itself checked: s4_evidence.validate() fails closed if a record's prose says BYTE-IDENTICAL and no other record carries the same captured bytes
refuted_round_5.note: code right, sentence wider than its evidence -- the dominant defect class in this program, and it does NOT move the verdict

s4_evidence_source.why: S4 used to be a dict literal inside this producer -- a claim living inside the thing that certifies it, undated, unattributed, and unable to say which BACKEND of a proxy answered. It is now committed data the producer reads, and load() fails closed when it is absent rather than degrading to 'no S4 evidence' (an absent source is zero signals, not one)
